Lesson: Welcome to the Media Lab: devices, files and folders
What learners do: Create a folder called `Media Lab — your name` with sub-folders: Design, Photo, Video, Writing, Portfolio; Rename three files with the pattern `2026-10-12_poster_v1.png`; Check the age rules for Canva and CapCut with your instructor (both expect 13+; younger members use the programme's supervised accounts)
Check: mcq: Which file name will you still understand in six months? | task: Upload a screenshot of your Media Lab folder with its five sub-folders.

Lesson: Staying safe online, and asking before you post
What learners do: Complete one Be Internet Awesome activity; Write three rules for your Creative Team about posting people's photos
Check: mcq: Before you post a photo of a friend at the centre, you should… | short: A stranger messages you offering to pay for your designs if you send your home address. What do you do?

Lesson: Researching online and checking your sources
What learners do: Research a local environmental problem and find three trustworthy sources; For each source, write who made it and why you trust it
Check: mcq: Which is the best first check of a website you have never heard of?

Lesson: AI tools: what they are and how to use them honestly
What learners do: Start the first chapter of Elements of AI; Ask an AI tool for five campaign slogans about clean streets, then improve the best one yourself and note what you changed
Check: mcq: You used an AI tool to draft a caption and then edited it. What should you do? | short: Name one thing AI tools often get wrong, and how you would check it.

Lesson: The creative process: from a brief to a finished piece
What learners do: Read the sample brief for a school notice; Sketch three thumbnail ideas on paper
Check: mcq: Why sketch several ideas before designing one?

Lesson: Creative Teams: roles and how we work together
What learners do: Meet your team and agree three team rules; Choose your first role — it rotates each month
Check: task: Upload your team's charter: members, first roles and three rules.

Lesson: Graphic design 1: Canva and visual hierarchy
What learners do: Do the Canva Design School beginner lesson; Recreate a poster you like to understand its structure
Check: mcq: What is visual hierarchy?

Lesson: Month 1 challenge: an environmental awareness poster set
What learners do: Plan the three posters as a team; Design them in Canva; Present them at the next session
Check: project: Upload your team's three posters and one paragraph explaining the message and who it is for. | reflection: What did you learn this month, and what will you do differently on the next challenge?

What learners do: Do the Canva colour lesson; Build a palette for an imaginary juice brand
Check: mcq: Light grey text on a white background is a problem because…

What learners do: Redesign a crowded flyer using only two fonts
Check: task: Upload your before-and-after flyer and name the two fonts you used.

What learners do: Use Canva's grid to rebuild a busy page
Check: mcq: White space in a design is…

Lesson: Composition: creating a social media graphic
What learners do: Design an Instagram post announcing a centre open day
Check: task: Upload your open-day post.

What learners do: Study two local brands and list their colours, fonts and tone
Check: short: Name three things a brand guide should include.

Lesson: Designing an invitation and a certificate
What learners do: Design an invitation and a certificate for a Media Lab event
Check: task: Upload your invitation and certificate.

What learners do: Write the brief for your event as a team; List every item you will deliver and who owns it
Check: task: Upload your team's task list: each item, its owner and its deadline.

Lesson: Month 2 challenge: a complete event branding package
What learners do: Finish and export every item; Present to the group and take feedback
Check: project: Upload your team's branding package (logo, palette, poster, social post, invitation, badge) and a one-page brand guide. | reflection: What did you learn this month, and what will you do differently on the next challenge?

What learners do: Turn on your phone camera's grid; Take five photographs of one object from different angles
Check: mcq: The rule of thirds suggests placing your subject…

What learners do: Take three photos of the same thing — in shade, in sunlight and against a window
Check: task: Upload your three photos and say which light worked best and why.

What learners do: Practise portraits of a teammate who agrees; Review the Lab's consent rules from week 1
Check: mcq: A parent at an event says they do not want their child photographed. You…

What learners do: Edit three of your photos in a free phone editor or Canva
Check: task: Upload one photo before and after editing, and list what you changed.

Lesson: Writing for media: captions, articles and slogans
What learners do: Write captions for three of your photos; Write a 150-word article about something at your centre
Check: short: Rewrite this caption to be clearer and more interesting: 'This is a picture of our class.'

What learners do: Plan a five-photo story about a person in your community (with their permission)
Check: task: Upload your story plan: the person, the problem, the change, and the five shots you need.

What learners do: Agree your story and shot list; Get permission from everyone who will appear
Check: task: Upload your shot list and confirmation that everyone pictured has agreed.

Lesson: Month 3 challenge: a community photo story
What learners do: Shoot, edit and caption your story; Present it at the next session
Check: project: Upload your team's photo story (5–8 photos with captions) and a short introduction. | reflection: What did you learn this month, and what will you do differently on the next challenge?

What learners do: Storyboard a one-minute 'day at the centre' video in six frames
Check: mcq: A storyboard is…

What learners do: Film the six shots from your storyboard
Check: task: Upload two of your clips and say what you did to keep them steady and the sound clear.

What learners do: Edit your clips into a one-minute video
Check: mcq: What is a 'cut' in video editing?

What learners do: Add music and subtitles to your one-minute video
Check: mcq: Why add subtitles? | task: Upload your finished one-minute video with subtitles.

What learners do: Write five open questions; Record a two-minute interview with a teammate
Check: short: Turn this closed question into an open one: 'Do you like the centre?'

What learners do: Choose your topic and storyboard; Arrange two interviews and get consent
Check: task: Upload your storyboard and interview plan, with consent confirmed.

What learners do: Edit your team's documentary rough cut; Swap rough cuts with another team for feedback
Check: task: Give another team written feedback on their rough cut: two things that work and one to improve.

Lesson: Month 4 challenge: a short community documentary
What learners do: Finish, subtitle and export; Present at the next session
Check: project: Upload your team's 2–3 minute documentary. | reflection: What did you learn this month, and what will you do differently on the next challenge?

Lesson: Social media: platforms, audiences and responsibility
What learners do: Compare how three organisations post on two platforms
Check: mcq: Posting for an organisation, you see a rude comment. The best first step is…

Lesson: Content strategy and a content calendar
What learners do: Make a one-week content calendar for the Media Lab's own page
Check: task: Upload your one-week content calendar: day, platform, post idea and goal.

What learners do: Analyse one campaign you like: audience, message, call to action
Check: mcq: A 'call to action' is…

What learners do: Generate ten caption ideas with an AI tool, pick and improve two, and note what you changed
Check: short: When is it NOT acceptable to use an AI-generated image in a campaign?

What learners do: Script and storyboard a 30-second promo for an NGG centre
Check: task: Upload your promo script and storyboard.

What learners do: Agree goal, audience and calendar; Assign graphics, video, captions and posting
Check: task: Upload your campaign plan: goal, audience, calendar and who makes what.

What learners do: Make every asset on your plan; Review each other's work against the brief
Check: task: Upload two assets you made and say how they follow the campaign's style.

Lesson: Month 5 challenge: a social media campaign with a promo video
What learners do: Finish all assets; Present the campaign and how you would measure success
Check: project: Upload your team's campaign: calendar, at least five graphics with captions, and the promo video. | reflection: What did you learn this month, and what will you do differently on the next challenge?

What learners do: Build a task board for your final project; Run a five-minute check-in: done, doing, stuck
Check: mcq: In a team check-in, the most useful thing to share is…

Lesson: Leading a team and mentoring a younger learner
What learners do: Teach a newer member one thing you learned (with your instructor); Note what you taught and how it went
Check: reflection: You taught a newer learner a skill. What went well, what was hard, and what would you do differently as a mentor?

What learners do: Choose six pieces from across the year; Write two sentences for each: the brief and what you did
Check: task: Upload a draft of your portfolio (a page or PDF) with at least six pieces and notes.

What learners do: Choose your story and the formats you will use; Agree roles — each member leads one part
Check: task: Upload your final project plan: the story, formats, roles and deadlines.

What learners do: Produce your part; Swap for peer review and improve
Check: task: Give a teammate written feedback on their part: two things that work and one to improve.

What learners do: Prepare your three-minute presentation; Rehearse with your team
Check: task: Upload your presentation outline: opening, the story, what you made, what you learned.

Lesson: Month 6 challenge: a community storytelling project
What learners do: Finish and submit every part
Check: project: Upload your team's community storytelling project (all parts) and a short introduction.

What learners do: Present your project and portfolio at the showcase; Write your next goal
Check: project: Upload your final portfolio link. | reflection: Looking back over the six months: what are you proudest of, what was hardest, and what is your next goal in the Lab?
